# Refactor guard: worklist split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `worklist.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an
unchanged public surface at `./worklist.js`, unmodified test files, no new
circular imports, and a single `WorkItemListState` declaration. Nothing in the
repo enforces these for `worklist.ts` today. The `downtime-worker` series
already built exactly this machinery for its own split
(`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` + `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`);
this child reuses it rather than duplicating it.

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-30, `dev`, `worklist.ts` = 7,899 lines):

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production
  (`index.ts` → `getTermSize`, `runWorklistTui`; `fetcher.ts` → `STAGES`,
  `Stage`) and 34 test files, of which **24** are `worklist*.test.ts` suites.
- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature
  (child WL-0MVND6MQS000L01W).
- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`
   (parent AC5), mirroring the `dispatchInFlightCount` gate.
5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and
   `downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` must stay **byte-identical and green** —
   duplicating the 28k-line scanner is not acceptable.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the
   untouched `downtime-worker` guard.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a
   `barrel`/`family`/`declarationName` target (defaults unchanged) in
   `isSplitFamilyFile`, `splitFamilyModules`, `findBarrelValueImports`,
   `findSplitFamilyCycles` and `findDispatchInFlightDeclarations`; add a
   `--target worklist` branch to the `--write-baseline` CLI.
2. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import … from './worklist.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes, dedupe, sort →
   `worklist.split-baseline.json` with provenance fields (expect 66 symbols).
3. Write `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` with the five gates (exports,
   single-owner, cycle/barrel, size+allowlist, baseline provenance), each as a
   separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
4. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   sources parsed by the same helpers) and assert each gate reports a failure.
5. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the guard's helper section so the final child
   (`WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N`) can empty it in one line.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — minimal parametrisation (defaults preserved)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — must stay unchanged and green

## Constraints

- Additive only: adding a test file and a parametrisation hook does not violate
  parent AC3 ("no test file is modified").
- No production `worklist*.ts` edits in this child — it lands first, alone.
- No new runtime dependencies (`typescript` is already used by `scan.ts`).

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- Precedent: `WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E` (downtime-worker split guard) — same shape,
  same AC numbering, already green on `dev`.

# Refactor guard: init split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ — decompose `src/commands/init.ts` god class
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Position in chain:** 1 of 7 — blocks every extraction child.

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `src/commands/init.ts` split, I want one automated
gate that fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so
that every extraction child can land safely, no existing test assertion changes,
and no reviewer has to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4 require: no file over 1,000 lines, an unchanged public
surface at `./init.js`, unmodified test assertions, and an acyclic import graph.
Nothing in the repo enforces this for `src/commands/init*.ts` today. This child
builds the enforcement first, mirroring `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G) and `tests/interview/split-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MVXY34A900816MN).

Facts captured at plan time (2026-11-03, `dev`):

- `src/commands/init.ts` — 1,515 lines; public surface is exactly
  **2 exports**: default `register(ctx: PluginContext)` and named
  `isSorraAgentsInstalled(): boolean`.
- Consumers of `./init.js`: `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import, default)
  and `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` (default import). No external consumer imports
  `isSorraAgentsInstalled`, but it must stay importable (parent AC2).
- Three brittle **source-text** tests in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` read
  `src/commands/init.ts` with `fs.readFileSync` and assert hook-content strings
  (`tmp-worktree`, `git-common-dir`, `git-dir`, `const postCheckoutContent`,
  two `const centralScriptContent` occurrences). Those tests will break when
  child 4 moves the hook generators to `init.hooks.ts`.
- `tests/cli/init.test.ts` (584 lines) and `tests/cli/initialization-check.test.ts`
  (201 lines) are black-box CLI tests; they do not import init internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** guard `tests/cli/init/split-guard.test.ts` passes on the
   current tree before any production code moves.
2. Committed baseline `tests/cli/init/init.split-baseline.json` records the two
   public exports (value/default flagged separately) plus provenance (generation
   command, source commit, timestamp).
3. Public exports from the original module path remain importable unchanged
   (barrel re-export where consumers exist): default `register` and named
   `isSorraAgentsInstalled` are still importable from `src/commands/init.js`.
4. No file (original or extracted module) exceeds 1,000 lines — the size gate
   enforces the ceiling for every `src/commands/init*.ts` production module,
   driven by an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains only
   `'init.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever shrinks.
5. No new circular imports; module responsibilities documented — no production
   `src/commands/init*.ts` module contains a runtime import of `./init.js`, and
   the static import graph of `init*.ts` modules is acyclic.
6. Hook-content gate: the concatenated `src/commands/init*.ts` family source
   still contains `tmp-worktree`, `git-common-dir`, `git-dir`,
   `const postCheckoutContent`, and two `const centralScriptContent` blocks —
   so the hook generators remain behaviour-preserving wherever they live.
7. All existing tests pass without modification to their import paths or
   assertions (move-only, behaviour-preserving) — the three source-text tests
   in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` are generalised to read the whole
   `src/commands/init*.ts` family (concatenated) instead of only `init.ts`.
   **Assertion logic is unchanged** — only the source location is generalised
   so the tests pass before and after child 4. This is the only existing-test
   edit in the epic (see OPEN QUESTION below).
8. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a removed
   hook-content string) — failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite.
10. A comment records the baseline generation command and the gate-to-parent-AC
    mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `tests/cli/init/split-guard-scan.ts`: list `src/commands/init*.ts`,
   concatenate their source, parse the public exports, load the baseline.
2. Add `tests/cli/init/split-guard.test.ts` with four separately named `it()`
   checks (public surface, size+allowlist, cycle/barrel, hook content) and
   negative-case fixtures.
3. Generate `tests/cli/init/init.split-baseline.json` (provenance: command,
   `git rev-parse HEAD`, ISO timestamp).
4. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the test helper so the finalise child empties
   it in one line.
5. Replace the three `new URL('../src/commands/init.ts', ...)` reads in
   `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` with the family-concatenation helper; keep
   every `expect(...)` assertion byte-identical.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the output in a comment.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/cli/init/split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `tests/cli/init/split-guard-scan.ts` — new
- `tests/cli/init/init.split-baseline.json` — new
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — source-location generalisation only (3 tests)
- `src/commands/init.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- OPEN QUESTION (recorded on the parent): parent AC3 says "without modification
  to their import paths or assertions". This child changes neither an import
  path nor an assertion — it generalises the file read from `init.ts` to the
  `init*.ts` family. Producer to confirm this reading, or choose the fallback
  (keep hook content constants in `init.ts` and extract only the install
  functions).

data.description:
## Problem statement

The GitHub integration (`wl gh push` / `wl gh import` paths) builds `gh` command strings with `JSON.stringify()` for user-provided text (issue titles, assignees, labels, label names/colours) and executes them through a shell (`runGh` via `execSync(..., { shell: '/bin/bash' })` and `runGhDetailed` via `execSync` with the default `/bin/sh`). `JSON.stringify()` escapes only the characters that are special *inside a JSON/JavaScript double-quoted string* — quotes, backslashes and control characters — but it does **not** escape `$`, backticks or `!`. When the JSON-quoted result is embedded in a shell double-quoted context, `$()`, backticks and `${…}` are still command/parameter substituted by the shell, so a work-item title, assignee or label containing e.g. `$(id)` or `` `whoami` `` is executed rather than passed through literally. This is a shell command-injection vector; the current `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md` incorrectly documents `JSON.stringify()` as "Safe — both provide equivalent protection".

## Users

- **Primary:** Worklog users who push locally-authored work items to GitHub. Any user who creates a title/assignee/label containing shell metacharacters (`$()`, backticks, `!`) could trigger unintended command execution on their machine when `wl gh push` runs.
- **Secondary:** Maintainers responsible for the security posture of the GitHub integration and for the accuracy of the shell-escaping policy documentation.

User stories:
- As a Worklog user, I want titles/assignees/labels I push to GitHub to be passed to `gh` literally, even when they contain `$`, backticks or `!`, so that pushing never executes unintended shell commands.
- As a maintainer, I want the GitHub command builders to use a single, proven shell-escaping primitive so that new command sites are safe by default and the documented policy is accurate.

## Existing state

- `src/github/transport.ts` — `runGh` executes via `execSync(command, { shell: '/bin/bash' })` (and `spawnSync('/bin/bash', ['-c', command])` for paginated commands); `runGhDetailed` executes via bare `execSync(command)` (default `/bin/sh`); `spawnCommand` uses `spawn('/bin/bash', ['-c', command])`. All are shell-interpreted.
- `src/github/issues.ts` — 13 `JSON.stringify(...)` interpolations: `--add-assignee` (×2, sync+async), `--title` (×3), `--add-label`/`--remove-label` (×6), all inside `gh issue …` command strings.
- `src/github/labels.ts` — 4 `JSON.stringify(...)` interpolations: `-f name=`/`-f color=` (×2 in `gh api … labels`) and `--color` via `gh issue label create` (×2 fallback).
- `src/shell-escape.ts` — provides `escapeShellArg(arg, platform?)` (POSIX single-quote wrapping with `'\''` escaping, Windows double-quote) and `quoteShellValue(value)` (POSIX-only single-quote wrapping). Single-quoting is safe against `$`, backticks, `!`, `;`, `|`, etc.
- `src/github/hierarchy.ts` and the GraphQL paths in `issues.ts` already use `quoteShellValue()` and are safe.
- `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md` currently lists `src/github/issues.ts` and `src/github/labels.ts` as "Safe" using `JSON.stringify()` and documents an "Exceptions" note asserting it is valid shell escaping — this claim is wrong and must be corrected.
- Test coverage: `tests/shell-escape.test.ts` (23 tests) covers `escapeShellArg`/`quoteShellValue`; no test asserts that the GitHub command builders are safe against `$()`/backtick/`!` payloads.

## Desired change

1. Triage every `JSON.stringify()`-into-shell site in `src/github/` (issues, labels; verify no others) to confirm whether untrusted/user-controlled text reaches the shell.
2. Replace confirmed vulnerable interpolations with `quoteShellValue()` (POSIX) or, preferably where the value is not a fixed-shape argument, pass values as argv to a non-shell API. Preserve the existing single-quote-wrapping for GraphQL paths.
3. Add regression tests proving that titles/assignees/labels containing `$()`, backticks, `!`, `;`, `|` are passed literally (not executed) by the affected command builders.
4. Correct `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md`: remove the "JSON.stringify() is safe" claim/exception and record the actual escaping primitive used.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All `JSON.stringify()` interpolations that flow into a shell-executed `gh` command string (`src/github/issues.ts`, `src/github/labels.ts`, and any other site found) are replaced with a shell-safe quoting primitive (`quoteShellValue()` / `escapeShellArg()`) or converted to argv/non-shell execution.
- [ ] A regression test (unit) proves that a title containing `$(touch /tmp/pwned)`, a backtick payload and a `!` payload are passed to `gh` literally and are **not** executed, across the affected create/edit/label command builders.
- [ ] `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md` no longer claims `JSON.stringify()` is safe shell escaping; the "Audited Files" table and "Exceptions" section reflect the actual escaping primitive (`quoteShellValue`) in the github modules.
- [ ] No regression in existing GitHub integration behaviour (`wl gh push`/`import` command construction unchanged for well-formed input); existing `tests/shell-escape.test.ts` and github test suites still pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- POSIX-only quoting (`quoteShellValue`) is acceptable for the GitHub integration because `runGh*` already invokes `/bin/bash` (or `/bin/sh`); the Windows branch of `escapeShellArg` is not required here but must not be broken.
- Changes must not alter the `gh` command *shape* expected by tests/mocks (e.g. label lists are still comma-joined before quoting).
- Do not weaken the existing safe paths (`hierarchy.ts`, GraphQL query escaping).
- Documentation changes must keep the policy accurate without over-claiming; correcting a false "safe" claim is in scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/github/issues.ts` — replace `JSON.stringify(...)` at `--add-assignee`, `--title`, `--add-label`, `--remove-label` with `quoteShellValue(...)` (or argv) across sync + async builders.
- `src/github/labels.ts` — replace `JSON.stringify(label)`, `JSON.stringify(color)` in `gh api … labels` and `gh issue label create` fallback with `quoteShellValue(...)`.
- `src/github/transport.ts` — verify `runGh`/`runGhDetailed` remain the only shell entry points; no change expected but re-confirm.
- `src/shell-escape.ts` — existing primitive; no change (unless a shared helper for comma-joined label lists is warranted).
- `tests/shell-escape.test.ts` and/or a new `tests/github-shell-escaping.test.ts` — add metacharacter regression tests.
- `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md` — correct the "Safe" claim and Exceptions section.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** user-controlled text (titles, assignees, labels) genuinely reaches these command strings via `wl gh push`/`import`. Confirmed by reading `workItemToIssuePayload`/`updateGithubIssue*` call sites; the implementer must re-confirm during triage that no upstream validation already neutralises metacharacters.
- **Risk — missed sites:** the grep is on `src/github/`; other modules (`src/github-sync.ts`, `src/github-pre-filter.ts`) may build commands too — triage must sweep `src/` for `JSON.stringify` adjacent to `runGh`/`execSync`/`spawn(... '-c' ...)`.
- **Risk — mock breakage:** existing tests may assert exact command strings containing JSON-quoted values; switching to single quotes will require updating those assertions (expected, benign).
- **Risk — comma-joined label lists:** `quoteShellValue(labels.join(','))` preserves the comma-joined shape; do not quote each label individually.
- **Risk — scope creep:** incidental improvements (e.g. converting all `gh` calls to argv-based execution) should be filed as linked follow-ups, not folded into this fix.
- **Failure mode:** over-eager quoting could double-quote values already validated as safe (repo slug, numeric issue numbers) — leave typed/validated values unquoted as today.

## Related work

- WL-0MP082Y1Q003GCUM — *Audit internal shell command construction for proper escaping of user text* (completed). This prior audit is what classified `JSON.stringify()` as safe; the current item corrects that specific classification. **Not a duplicate** — the prior audit's conclusion was wrong for shell-command contexts, and this item owns the fix.
- WL-0MVVLY0QW007L9ZB — *Document github module layout* (completed; discovered-from source). The docs update there points at the owning modules but preserved the "safe" wording; this item owns correcting that claim.
- `WL-0MVGKGR2H006MNVG` — `src/github.ts` decomposition epic (the modules named here are the decomposition children).
- WL-0MOZUVGL6008QV45 — *Prevent shell command substitution in wl audit text updates* (prior related escaping fix; same class of bug).

## Duplicate-work detection

`wl search "shell escaping github"` performed. Candidates reviewed:
- WL-0MP082Y1Q003GCUM (completed) — partial overlap only: it audited escaping broadly but concluded `JSON.stringify()` was safe. Its ACs are **not** fully satisfied here (it did not fix the `bash -c` substitution issue). Proceeding with this item as the gap-closer; linked as related.
- No other overlapping completed item found.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required — the seed description (written while updating `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md`) already contained a precise problem statement, the exact affected call sites, the proposed remediation (`quoteShellValue` / argv), and the documentation correction scope. Repo inspection confirmed the locations and the safety claim in `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MP082Y1Q003GCUM** – Audit internal shell command construction for proper escaping of user text (completed)
- **WL-0MVVLY0QW007L9ZB** – Document github module layout (completed)
- **WL-0MW0JF7QN007E1JU** – Extract github-sync label resolution (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: accept, add, affected, argv, ask (+68 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: accept, add, affected, ask, assignee (+62 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: accept, add, argv, ask, assignee (+59 more)

data.description:
**Headline:** recover tool calls a model leaks as plain text — fix the assistant
message so Pi executes the intended call in the same turn, and fall back to one
bounded corrective continue when the leaked call cannot be safely reconstructed.

## Problem statement

Models served by the Local Proxy occasionally emit a **tool call as plain text**
(`<response>` / `<tool_call>` / `<function=NAME>` / `<parameter=KEY>` markup)
instead of a structured `toolCall` content block. Pi renders the markup in the
TUI, executes nothing for it, and the turn ends — so an unattended agent (audit,
implement, downtime-dispatch panes) silently stalls mid-workflow, or half-executes
a batch when only some of the intended calls parsed.

The shape seen on the Pi TUI (operator report, 2026-11-03):

```text
<response>

 <tool_call>
 <function=read>
 <parameter=path>
 /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md
 </parameter>
 </function>
 </tool_call><tool_call>
 <function=bash>
 <parameter=command>
 cd /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub && wl show WL-0MVGKGU19004NTHB --json 2>&1
 </parameter>
 </function>
 </tool_call>
```

Nothing in that block runs: Pi has no `toolCall` content block to execute, so the
next turn depends on the model noticing its own text.

## Users

- **Unattended agents in herdr panes** (audit / implement / downtime dispatch).
  Story: *"As an unattended agent, when the model leaks a tool call as text, I
  want the intended call to still run — or one corrective retry — instead of my
  session quietly ending mid-workflow."*
- **The operator watching the pane.** Story: *"As the operator, I want a visible
  one-line warning when a leaked call was recovered or a retry was issued, so I
  can tell a recovered session from a stuck one."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Detect and repair.** For an assistant message whose `text` content contains
   Hermes/Qwen-style tool-call markup, the extension appends a structured
   `{ type: "toolCall", id, name, arguments }` block (setting `stopReason:
   "toolUse"`), preserves every other message field, and replaces the leaked
   markup with a one-line note (e.g. `[recovered tool call: read(path=/…)]`).
   Unit tests cover: complete block, multiple blocks, `<tool_call>` opener
   missing (the shape observed live), missing closers, plain text containing no
   markup (untouched), and a recovered call identical to an already-parsed
   `toolCall` (dropped as a duplicate).
2. **Never execute a truncated call.** If any `<parameter=KEY>` value is
   unterminated, or the parsed tool name is not in `pi.getActiveTools()`, no
   `toolCall` is synthesised and the fallback (AC3) is used instead — a
   half-streamed `bash` command must never run. Covered by unit tests.
3. **Bounded corrective-continue fallback.** When repair is skipped, the
   extension injects a corrective `custom_message` at the `turn_end` boundary
   naming the missed call(s) and requests exactly one continuation
   (`continue: true`). It never fires twice for the same assistant message,
   never when that message already produced tool results, and stops after a
   configurable session cap (default 5). Covered by unit tests.
4. **Execution contract proven, not assumed.** The in-place `message_end`
   replacement is real in the code (`agent-session.js` →
   `_replaceMessageInPlace`, before `agent-loop.js` reads
   `content.filter(c => c.type === "toolCall")`) but is **not** stated in the Pi
   extension docs. An integration test therefore drives `runAgentLoop` from the
   repo's pinned `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` with a fake stream that emits
   the leaked markup, and asserts the recovered tool executes exactly once — and
   fails if the repair is bypassed. This test is the early-warning tripwire for a
   future Pi upgrade changing the contract.
5. **Observable and non-interfering.** Each repair or fallback emits exactly one
   `ctx.ui.notify(..., "warning")` naming the recovered call(s). Messages with no
   markup produce no action and no notification; aborted runs are untouched; a
   parser/handler exception is caught and degrades to today's behaviour (turn
   ends as before) without breaking the session.
6. **Tests.** New unit, wiring (mocked `ExtensionAPI`) and integration tests, each
   asserting behaviour, all passing in the changed-scope gate.
7. **Documentation.** `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` (Error Recovery Module
   section) documents detection, repair, the fallback, the bounds, the settings
   constants and the Pi-version dependency noted in AC4; code comments record the
   contract at the `message_end` handler.
8. **Full project test suite** must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Extension-side only (`packages/tui/extensions/`); no changes to Pi itself, no
  changes to the `llm-manager` proxy repo (repo boundary).
- No new runtime dependencies: `node:crypto` for call ids; ESM `.js` import
  specifiers per the extension's existing convention.
- Must behave in print / JSON / RPC modes where `ctx.ui.notify` and `setStatus`
  are no-ops (same graceful-degradation standard as the activity indicator).
- Must not disturb the existing recovery module: `suppressBuiltinRetry`,
  `retryStates`, `interruptibleState` and the parse-error/compaction paths keep
  their current behaviour; an aborted run
  (`interruptibleState.userAborted`) is never repaired or continued.
- Repair must be idempotent: a repaired message contains no markup, so replaying
  the handler cannot re-add calls.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/` already owns the "the turn went
  wrong, recover it" surface: `error-patterns.ts` (classification),
  `recovery.ts` (`executeParseErrorContinue`, compact-and-continue),
  `register-recovery.ts` (`agent_end` dispatch, `/retry`, turn state) and
  `settings.test.ts` (config defaults). The precedent for a single-shot
  auto-continue is `WL-0MSNKWLER003EGE0` (JSON parse errors).
- No `message_end` handler exists in the extension today, and nothing inspects
  assistant `text` content for tool-call markup.
- **Behaviour today (no extension):** the markup is shown as assistant text, no
  tool runs, and the run ends as if the model had finished its answer. Some models
  self-correct on the following turn (observed in the 2026-09-17 case), which is
  why this is intermittent rather than a hard stop.
- Evidence in the local session corpus (1,316 sessions scanned): exactly one
  assistant message leaked the markup — 2026-09-17, model `plan` (Local Proxy) —
  and it carried **one valid `toolCall` plus a leaked
  `<function=read>…</function></tool_call>` fragment**, i.e. the failure is
  partial as well as total. The operator's `<response>`/two-block example is the
  same chat-template leak shape.
- Version note: Pi's extension docs do not describe `message_end` replacement as a
  way to add tool calls, but both the globally installed Pi (1.5.x) and the
  repo's pinned dev dependency (0.79.10) apply the replacement in place before
  the loop filters tool calls.

## Desired change

A new recovery capability, `leaked tool call recovery`, in the Worklog Pi
extension:

1. **Pure logic module** `lib/recovery/leaked-tool-call.ts`: dialect patterns
   (Hermes/Qwen XML: `<response>`, `<tool_call>`, `<function=NAME>`,
   `<parameter=K>`, tolerant of a missing opener or missing closers), a parser
   returning `{ name, arguments, complete }`, a message transformer
   (`repairAssistantMessage`) and the bound/guard policy. No Pi imports, so it is
   unit-testable.
2. **Registration** `lib/recovery/register-leaked-tool-call.ts`, called from
   `Worklog/index.ts` beside `registerRecoveryModule`:
   - `message_end` → parse + repair + notify (AC1, AC2, AC5).
   - `turn_end` → corrective `{ entries, continue: true }` fallback with bounds
     (AC3).
   - `session_start` → reset the per-session counters.
3. **Tests**: unit (`leaked-tool-call.test.ts`), wiring
   (`register-leaked-tool-call.test.ts`, mocked `pi.on`), integration
   (`leaked-tool-call.execution.test.ts` driving `runAgentLoop` with a fake
   stream — AC4).
4. **Docs**: `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` Error Recovery Module section.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/leaked-tool-call.ts` — New: dialect patterns, parser, `repairAssistantMessage`, bounds/settings constants.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/leaked-tool-call.test.ts` — New: parser + transformer unit tests (AC1, AC2).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-leaked-tool-call.ts` — New: `message_end` repair wiring, `turn_end` fallback, `session_start` reset.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-leaked-tool-call.test.ts` — New: wiring tests with a mocked `ExtensionAPI` (AC3, AC5).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/leaked-tool-call.execution.test.ts` — New: `runAgentLoop` integration test proving the recovered call executes (AC4).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` — Register the new module next to `registerRecoveryModule`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — Reference only: keep `interruptibleState`/turn-state behaviour intact (no behaviour change expected).
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — Document the capability, bounds and settings.

## Related work

- WL-0MSNKWLER003EGE0 — Auto-recover from JSON parse errors in audit processing (completed). Direct precedent: single-shot "continue" recovery on a malformed model output, no backoff loop.
- WL-0MR5QR1790034LXA — Fix: Auto-continue after compaction for max output tokens (CONTEXT_LENGTH) (completed). Same auto-continue machinery, different trigger.
- WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O — Auto-continue after mid-session compaction (session_compact event handling) (completed). Boundary/continuation plumbing precedent.
- WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK — Add Guardrails to Protect Worklog Data Integrity (completed). House style for `tool_call` interception in this extension (blocking, not repairing).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — undocumented contract drift.** `message_end` replacement + in-place
  mutation is read from Pi's source, not its docs; a Pi upgrade could stop
  executing appended tool calls. *Mitigation:* AC4's integration test fails loudly;
  the documented `turn_end` fallback keeps the session recoverable either way.
- **Risk — executing a mis-parsed call.** A truncated `bash` command would be
  dangerous. *Mitigation:* AC2 (unterminated parameter ⇒ never execute) and the
  active-tool-name allow list.
- **Risk — loop.** Repair + continue could ping-pong. *Mitigation:* repair is
  idempotent (markup stripped) and both paths share a session cap (default 5),
  with a warning notification on each event.
- **Risk — false positives** on legitimate prose that quotes such markup (docs,
  tests, this repo's own README). *Mitigation:* require a `<function=NAME>` block
  with at least one parameter and an active tool name; require the enclosing
  assistant message to be a completed turn with no matching executed call.
- **Assumption — dialect scope.** Only the Hermes/Qwen XML dialect is in scope
  (operator answer, Q3); patterns are a module-level list so `<|tool_call|>`,
  `to=functions.NAME` and fenced-JSON dialects are a config addition later.
- **Assumption — operator visibility.** Enabled by default; every recovery is
  announced with a `warning` notification (silent repair was not chosen).
- **Assumption — root cause is upstream.** The leak comes from the Local Proxy's
  chat template / tool-call parser for the served open-weight model; this work
  item is the agent-side safety net, not the cure. A `discovered-from` follow-up
  for the proxy side is optional and not part of these ACs.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Per-model leak statistics, a settings UI toggle, and
  proxy-side repair are out of scope; file them as separate items if wanted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (approach).** *"Which recovery approach — (A) intercept at `message_end`
  and repair the message so Pi executes the call in-turn with a corrective-continue
  fallback; (B) corrective continue only; (C) A without fallback?"*
  — Answer (operator): **A**. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-03.
  Research note: feasible — `agent-session.js` `_replaceMessageInPlace` mutates
  the finalized message in place during the `message_end` extension event, and
  `agent-loop.js` filters `toolCall` blocks from that message afterwards (verified
  in both Pi 1.5.x and the repo's pinned 0.79.10).
- **Q2 (leaked text handling).** *"What should happen to the leaked XML text in
  the conversation — (i) replace with a one-line note, (ii) keep raw markup,
  (iii) drop it?"* — Answer (operator): **i**. Source: interactive reply,
  2026-11-03.
- **Q3 (dialect scope).** *"Which dialects should detection cover — (1)
  XML/Hermes only, tolerant of truncated fragments; (2) also `<|tool_call|>`,
  `to=functions.NAME`, fenced JSON; (3) XML/Hermes closed blocks only?"*
  — Answer (operator): **1**. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-03.
- **Q4 (implicit, operator instruction).** *"Create a work item for this."*
  — Answer (operator): created as `WL-0MW0WBWY3006LQ8W` (this item). Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-03.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MR5QR1790034LXA** – Fix: Auto-continue after compaction for max output tokens (CONTEXT_LENGTH) (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5JBV0054CBY** – End-to-end test for detail view shortcut result handling (completed)
- **WL-0MKXK36KJ1L2ADCN** – Enhanced OpenCode Progress Feedback in TUI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: aborted, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+378 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: aborted, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+367 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: ac2, action, active, activity, add (+321 more)

**Headline:** Edge-case hardening of the leaked-tool-call parser and repair transformer — the full detection matrix, false-positive guards and idempotence. Parent: WL-0MW0WBWY3006LQ8W. Depends on the tracer-bullet slice.

## Goal

The tracer slice proves the end-to-end path on the live shape. This slice makes detection trustworthy: every documented dialect variance either parses correctly or is explicitly rejected, so a truncated or quoted block can never be executed and a legitimate message is never rewritten.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dialect matrix.** The parser handles, with a test per case: multiple blocks in one message; a missing `<tool_call>`/`<response>` opener (the shape observed live); missing `</function>`/`</tool_call>` closers; indentation/blank-line variance; adjacent blocks with no separator; and the operator's exact `<response>` sample from the parent item, kept as a fixture.
2. **Rejection matrix (parent AC2).** Zero calls are synthesised, and `complete: false` is reported, when a `<parameter=KEY>` value is unterminated, the parsed name is absent from the active-tool list, the block has no parameters, or the markup appears inside a fenced code span / quoted prose (false-positive guard for docs, READMEs and tests). Each case is asserted to yield no appended `toolCall` and an unchanged `stopReason`.
3. **Duplicate suppression.** A parsed call identical (name and arguments) to an already-parsed `toolCall` in the same message is dropped, and the replacement note lists only the calls actually recovered (parent AC1 case).
4. **Idempotence.** `repairAssistantMessage` on already-repaired output is a strict no-op: no markup, no new calls, no second note; asserted by applying the transformer twice and comparing deep equality.
5. **Test matrix.** `leaked-tool-call.test.ts` covers every case in AC1–AC4 with explicit expectations plus the markup-free-prose-untouched case, and the changed-scope gate is green with the existing recovery tests unmodified.
6. **Settings.** `LEAKED_TOOL_CALL_CONFIG` (`enabled`, `sessionCap` default 5, note template, corrective continuation prompt) lives in `leaked-tool-call.ts` and a unit test asserts the defaults, so the fallback slice and the docs slice consume one source of truth.

## Minimal implementation

- Keep the pattern list at module scope (additive dialect support later) and extend the parser to report `complete` plus a reason (`truncated-parameter`, `unknown-tool`, `no-parameters`, `quoted`).
- Add a fenced-code/quoted-prose guard before parsing.
- Add duplicate comparison against existing `toolCall` blocks (name + deep-equal arguments).
- Extend the fixture set with the operator sample and a truncated `bash` sample.
- Add the config object and its default-assertion test.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/leaked-tool-call.ts` — Extend: rejection reasons, false-positive guard, duplicate suppression, `LEAKED_TOOL_CALL_CONFIG`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/leaked-tool-call.test.ts` — Extend: full matrix + idempotence + config defaults.

## Constraints

- No behaviour change to the repair success path proven by the tracer slice (same note format, same appended block shape).
- Pure logic only — no Pi imports, no I/O, no timers; unit-testable in isolation.
- Must not disturb `register-recovery.ts` or the tripwire test from the tracer slice.

## Deliverables

Extended parser/transformer code, the full unit-test matrix, and exported config defaults.

## Related work

- Parent WL-0MW0WBWY3006LQ8W AC1/AC2; tracer slice (C1).
